items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: For me the very first jazz piano album I can recall hearing was an album my piano teacher brought me, it was a ten inch MGM LP called “You’re Hearing George Shearing.” ... I want to hear more of this music. And so I listened to a lot of Shearing then

ctx.x: Who were the pianists that affected or influenced your playing, or were there any?

Oh yeah. I mean I think most musicians start off being mostly affected by people on their instrument and then they expand their auditory interests. For me the very first jazz piano album I can recall hearing was an album my piano teacher brought me, it was a ten inch MGM LP called “You’re Hearing George Shearing.” And I remember hearing that album and saying woo, who is this guy? Listen to that marvelous classical technique and yet there’s this wonderful rhythmic thing going and he’s improvising, and I want to…

on the near west side. And again, because I was tall I could get in there, and I remember just spending nights listening to the Billy Taylor Trio and it just was wonderful music. Then I got a chance to hear Oscar Peterson at the London House in Chicago, which used to be a wonderful supper club. And I remember not only being knocked out by Oscar but even more so by Ray Brown, just the force and the drive of that playing, and I was thinking gee I hope someday I can play with a bass player like that. So I would say…
